text: Dietary fat is classified into two basic categories: saturated fatty acids (SFAs), which have a hydrogen atom on both sides of every carbon atom (i.e., the carbons are saturated with hydrogens), and unsaturated fatty acids, which contain one or more double bonds in their carbon chain (i.e., a missing hydrogen atom along the carbon chain). Fats with one double bond are called monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFAs), of which oleate is the most common. Fats with two or more double bonds are called polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs). There are two primary classes of PUFAs: omega-6 linoleate (also called omega-6 or n -6 fatty acids ) and omega-3 alpha-linolenate (also called omega-3 or n -3 fatty acids ).
